title: Comparison of two different non-invasive ventilation strategies, non-invasive intermittent positive pressure ventilation (NIPPV) and continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) in preterm infants using electrical impedance tomography (EIT), transcutaneous CO2 and O2 saturation measurement - a randomized clinical trial.
summary:
This study compares the non-invasive ventilation methods NIPPV and CPAP in premature infants with respiratory distress syndrome (ANS). 
The aim is to use electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to visualise lung ventilation and volumes, as well as oxygenation and ventilation using O2 and CO2 measurements, so that lung-protective respiratory support can be ensured.
As part of a cross-over study, one patient at a time is measured and observed for a period of four hours, randomising which form of ventilation is used at the start. During this period, the patient switches between NIPPV and CPAP mode every hour, so that each mode is used for a total of two hours. 
During this time, the breathing behaviour is continuously observed, documented and evaluated. Attention is also paid to changes in breathing frequency as well as the duration and occurrence of apnoeas. The evaluation focuses on the assessment of lung ventilation and volumes using the EIT measurement results, as well as the transcutaneous CO2 values, oxygen saturation (SpO2) and oxygen demand (FiO2).

interventions.name:
Premature babies (birth weight <1500g) who are treated in the neonatal intensive care unit at Giessen University Hospital and require non-invasive ventilation (CPAP/NIPPV) (FiO2 at 0.21-0.6 and a PEEP of 5-8 cmH2O).
Randomized allocation: Start CPAP for one hour, then switch to NIPPV for one hour.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.premature babies (birth weight <1500g) who are treated in the neonatal intensive care unit at Giessen University Hospital
2.need for non-invasive ventilation (CPAP/NIPPV)
3.FiO2 under CPAP/NIPPV at 0.21-0.6 with a PEEP of 5-8 cmH2O
4.at least 4 hypoxaemias (< 80% SpO2) and/or 4 apnoeas/bradycardias in 12 hours prior to study entry
5.written consent of the legal guardian has been obtained
Exclusion criteria:
1.premature and newborn infants with severe malformations that significantly impair respiratory regulation (severe CNS malformations), lung function (e.g. lung hypoplasia, acute extra-alveolar air such as pneumothorax and pulmonary interstitial emphysema, diaphragmatic hernias) or circulatory function (congenital cyanotic heart disease, severe septic shock), as well as periventricular leukomalacia and intraventricular haemorrhage (grade III and IV)
2.postnatal age <72h (often acute deterioration in the early phase of respiratory distress syndrome and to protect the minimal handling principle in the critical phase to prevent intraventricular haemorrhage)
3.clinical sepsis (defined as CRP value >10mg/l) with and without circulatory insufficiency or positive blood culture
4.anticipated blood transfusion or surgery during the study phase
